A test report supplied by the user described a P&T + lubrication test of Dana 755 Front Agri Axle, part number 10145957, M2 21V CVT, using Total/ELF Tractelf SF3 oil with the central oil fill reduced by 0.5 L. The report lists the test completion date as June 7, 2021, and test dates as April 7–8, 2021. The test ran at up to 3234 rpm (equivalent to 53 km/h), in forward and reverse, with power-loss checks at ambient temperature, 60°C, and 90°C, plus a two-hour P&T run and lubrication checks.

The report’s summary gives forward power loss after run-in as 3.60 kW at 90°C, 4.2 kW at 60°C, and 8.1 kW at ambient temperature; parenthetical comparison values are 4.55, 5.7, and 10.3 kW respectively. A results table elsewhere in the report instead lists 5.2 kW at 60°C, with 5.7 kW in parentheses, so the report contains a discrepancy. It states reverse power loss was lower than forward power loss.

During the P&T run, the report records about 85°C and 2.8 kW at 1 hour 6 minutes, followed by a power-loss step-up and lack of stabilization; at 2 hours it records about 110°C and 5.3 kW. The central oil temperature remained below the 120°C maximum allowable limit within the two-hour target.

The report rated the test partially passed: power loss improved relative to reference tests, but the P&T curves became irregular after 1 hour 6 minutes, with a power-loss step-up and no stabilization. Horizontal lubrication checks found no lubrication problems, and oil levels remained above the minimum in all compartments. Inclined lubrication testing was not performed because a suitable bench was unavailable. No oil leak or other lubrication problem was reported; the report advised against further oil reduction until the power-loss step-up is resolved.

The user asked for relevant test-scope and result measures from a technical report to be presented in a labeled table with values and units, followed by a summary and conclusions. The assistant returned selected power-loss and P&T temperature/power values and summarized the partial pass, irregular curves, and satisfactory lubrication findings.
